page.overview:
What is Agna Qel'a?

The history of the city of Agna Qel'a spans a long time, In contrast, Atka claimed in "The Executioner's Blade" that the city was mere "centuries" old by the era of Roku. Conversely, Atka was heavily biased against Agna Qel'a and greatly downplayed the city's importance and status before the era of Roku, so it is unclear whether her claim regarding the settlement's age was reliable.|group = nb}} being founded after the North Pole's independent tribes resolved to unify. The city was built as a symbol of the unification, and to facilitate the intra-tribal relations. However, the spirit of Agna Qel'a's foundation was maintained, and the city remained an open port city welcoming to all visitors for much of its history. Initially, Agna Qel'a's importance was largely restricted to its position as a political meeting place and the location of religious pilgrimages. Over time, hunters also began to exchange their goods with local and foreign traders at the settlement, though the city's economic status remained limited during its early history.

By the era of Yangchen, Agna Qel'a had grown into a prosperous and large settlement, its ice-crafted architecture a marvel to behold. Yangchen repeatedly visited the city during her early Avatar career, mostly concerning diplomatic and spiritual missions. The capital would maintain and grow its status over the following centuries.

In the late 4th century BG, Agna Qel'a celebrated the official revelation that Kuruk, a Northerner, was the new Avatar with a grand feast. Years later, when Kuruk wanted to marry Ummi at the Spirit Oasis, Koh the Face Stealer lured her into the Spirit World to punish Kuruk for neglecting his Avatar duties. In 296 BG, the famous firebending instructor and Fire Nation ex-official Hei-Ran was brought to Agna Qel'a for medical treatment. She spent the next year in the city, nursed back to health by the healer Atuat. By this time, the city had become a major economic hub.

In the 1st century BG, the city benefited from the growth of international trade and technological exchange, and came to house several powerful companies. Many people of the North's traditionally nomadic, rural sub-tribes migrated to Agna Qel'a during this period, seeking a more prosperous life. The population of the city exploded, This development was bolstered by the policies of Chief Tiguaa and his father before him, who greatly favored Agna Qel'a over the rest of the Northern Water Tribe, as they believed that their people's future was linked to trade and urbanism. However, this increase in trade also led to a rise in diseases, including the Northern Pox. Many people came to Agna Qel'a seeking treatment for the illness, with at times dozens asking for the cure in a single day. Chief Tiguaa agreed to supply the cure only if people were able to cover the cost, forcing many Earth Kingdom villages to go without treatment.
